Explanation: The core value unit is a piece of content placed into Facebook’s distribution system: a text post, photo, video, Reel, Story or other shareable post that can reach friends, followers or people selected by recommendation systems.

Meta Platforms owns and operates Facebook. This case models only Facebook’s Feed and Reels social-discovery layer, so the Owner governs Facebook’s ranking, creator rules, moderation and advertising inventory rather than the whole Meta product family.
Facebook has to keep people returning for relationships, communities and content while making the feed useful even when a user’s friend graph alone does not provide enough interesting material.
More useful discovery increases time, engagement and ad opportunities, while creator monetization can attract more supply of original content.
Facebook must balance recommendation quality, social relevance, spam, impersonation, harmful content and regulatory pressure without making the product feel disconnected from real relationships.
Facebook receives content, relationship and engagement signals, ranks posts into personalized feeds and monetizes part of that attention with advertising.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Attention / Signals — Users contribute attention, reactions, follows, hides, shares and relationship signals that Facebook uses to personalize ranking. | → Consumer · Feed / Recs — Facebook returns a personalized mix of connected content and AI-recommended posts, while also offering friend-only and other dedicated surfaces. | ← Provider · Posts / Reels — Creators and ordinary users supply the content that Facebook can distribute through Feed, Reels, Groups and related surfaces. | → Provider · Reach / Payout — Facebook provides distribution, audience feedback, creator tools and, for eligible creators, performance-based monetization. | ← Partner · Ad Spend — Marketers submit budgets, objectives and creative to compete for paid distribution around user attention. | → Partner · Reach / Results — Facebook delivers ad impressions, clicks and conversion-oriented outcomes, together with measurement and optimization tools.

Explanation: Facebook sets recommendation eligibility, originality rules, content standards, account enforcement, ad policies and user controls over what appears in Feed and Reels.
Facebook’s own Feed, Reels, notifications, search and sharing surfaces distribute content and pull people back into the network.
Core activities include content ranking, recommendation, moderation, integrity enforcement, creator monetization, ad delivery and experimentation with feed design.
Facebook relies on the social graph, content corpus, engagement signals, creator ecosystem, advertiser demand and large-scale AI ranking and ads systems.

Consumers are people who open Facebook to connect with people they know, participate in communities and discover posts, videos and Reels. The same person can later become a Provider by publishing content.
Users want to stay connected with people and communities they care about while also finding interesting content beyond their existing network.
A useful feed mixes social updates, community posts and recommendations that feel timely and personally relevant without requiring the user to search for everything.
Users can face repetitive recommendations, spam, unwanted content, misinformation, addictive design concerns and uncertainty about why particular posts appear.
Users contribute attention and behavioral signals through viewing, liking, commenting, sharing, following, hiding and messaging around content.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Attention / Signals — Users contribute attention, reactions, follows, hides, shares and relationship signals that Facebook uses to personalize ranking. | ← Owner · Feed / Recs — Facebook returns a personalized mix of connected content and AI-recommended posts, while also offering friend-only and other dedicated surfaces.

Explanation: The main Feed mixes connected and recommended content, while the dedicated Friends tab provides a friend-only view without recommended content.
People enter through the Facebook app or website and move among Feed, Reels, Groups, Friends and other Facebook surfaces.
Users scroll, watch, react, comment, share, follow, join groups, hide content and tune recommendations through their behavior and controls.
Users contribute identity and relationship data, follows, interests, engagement history, device and activity signals that help Facebook personalize distribution.

Providers include ordinary users, group members, Pages and professional creators who publish the posts that Facebook distributes. “Creators” is used as an umbrella term because the same user can consume content in one moment and supply it in the next.
Creators want their posts to reach friends, communities, followers or new audiences and, for professional creators, potentially generate income.
Recommendation can distribute strong content beyond an existing follower graph, while monetization programs can turn qualified views and engagement into creator income.
Creators face ranking uncertainty, changing recommendation rules, spam competition, impersonation and the risk that unoriginal or policy-violating content is deprioritized or demonetized.
Creators upload posts and Reels, add context or metadata and make them eligible for distribution to connected or recommended audiences.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Posts / Reels — Creators and ordinary users supply the content that Facebook can distribute through Feed, Reels, Groups and related surfaces. | ← Owner · Reach / Payout — Facebook provides distribution, audience feedback, creator tools and, for eligible creators, performance-based monetization.

Explanation: Facebook evaluates recommendation eligibility, originality, policy compliance, spam signals and integrity risks before or after distribution.
Supply enters through personal profiles, Professional Mode, Pages, Groups and creator publishing tools.
Creators produce posts, photos, video and Reels, respond to audiences, manage communities and use performance or monetization tools.
Creators contribute original content, voice, expertise, community relationships and existing follower or group audiences.

Marketers are the commercial side that pays Facebook for access to user attention. They are modelled as Partner rather than Provider because they do not supply the core Post that users come to consume; they fund the platform by buying targeted ad distribution around that content.
Marketers want to reach likely customers efficiently, measure outcomes and turn Facebook attention into awareness, leads, app activity or sales.
Facebook combines audience signals, AI ranking and ad auctions to help marketers find relevant audiences and optimize toward business outcomes.
Advertisers face auction competition, changing privacy rules, measurement limits, creative fatigue and uncertainty about incremental performance.
Marketers submit campaigns, creative, budgets and objectives; Facebook auctions and distributes ads into eligible attention opportunities.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Ad Spend — Marketers submit budgets, objectives and creative to compete for paid distribution around user attention. | ← Owner · Reach / Results — Facebook delivers ad impressions, clicks and conversion-oriented outcomes, together with measurement and optimization tools.

Explanation: Ads must meet policy and eligibility rules, then compete in auctions where predicted value, quality and advertiser bids shape delivery.
Businesses buy and manage campaigns through Meta Ads Manager and related business tools that can distribute ads across Facebook and other Meta placements.
Marketers define audiences and objectives, produce creative, set budgets, monitor delivery and evaluate conversions or other outcomes.
They contribute advertising spend, campaign goals, product information, creative assets and conversion signals.
